question: Which of the following was designated as the 58th Tiger Reserve of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhav National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madhav National Park** was designated as the **58th Tiger Reserve of India** in 2023, under the Project Tiger initiative, which aims to conserve tigers and their habitats.
 
• Madhav National Park is located in the **Shivpuri District of Madhya Pradesh**, a state known for its significant contribution to tiger conservation in India.
 
• This designation is part of the Indian government’s effort to expand the network of protected areas for tigers and strengthen biodiversity conservation.
 
• The park spans over an area of approximately **354 square kilometers**, making it an ideal habitat for tigers and other wildlife species.
 
• The inclusion of Madhav National Park as a tiger reserve reflects the government’s commitment to achieving conservation goals under the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Madhav National Park:**

 
 
• Madhav National Park was established in **1959** and is one of the oldest national parks in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is named after **Madhav Rao Scindia**, a prominent figure from the royal family of Gwalior.
 
• The park is home to a variety of wildlife, including **Tigers, Leopards, Indian Gazelle (Chinkara), and Nilgai**.
 
• It also features two important water bodies, **Sakhya Sagar Lake** and **Chandrashila Lake**, which provide water resources for the animals and act as tourist attractions.
 
• The park’s vegetation is primarily dry deciduous forest, interspersed with grasslands, creating an ideal environment for predators and prey.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched in **1973**, Project Tiger is a flagship conservation initiative of the Government of India, aiming to protect tigers and their natural habitats.
 
• The project is implemented by the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** and has led to the establishment of **tiger reserves** across the country.
 
• India is home to approximately **70% of the global tiger population**, and the project has been pivotal in increasing tiger numbers through scientific management and anti-poaching measures.
 
• The latest All-India Tiger Estimation Report of **2022** recorded a significant increase in tiger population, emphasizing the success of such initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Reserves in Madhya Pradesh:**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is known as the **"Tiger State of India"** due to its high tiger population and the presence of multiple tiger reserves.
 
• Notable reserves include **Kanha Tiger Reserve, Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve, Panna Tiger Reserve, Satpura Tiger Reserve**, and now **Madhav National Park**.
 
• The state’s tiger reserves contribute significantly to eco-tourism and conservation education.
 
 
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):**
 
 
• The NTCA was established in **2006** under the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 to strengthen tiger conservation efforts in India.
 
• It provides funding, technical support, and policy guidance for tiger reserves and ensures adherence to conservation protocols.
 
• The authority also conducts periodic assessments of tiger populations and their habitats.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh** has consistently ranked among the top states in India for tiger conservation efforts, earning national and international recognition.
 
• The designation of Madhav National Park as the **58th Tiger Reserve** aligns with the objectives of the **Global Tiger Initiative**, a worldwide effort to double tiger populations by 2022.
 
• The park’s location near urban centers like Gwalior and Shivpuri increases its potential for eco-tourism and awareness programs.
 
• The involvement of local communities in conservation activities under the NTCA framework ensures sustainable management and reduces human-wildlife conflict.
 
• Continuous monitoring and capacity-building initiatives are crucial for the long-term success of tiger reserves like Madhav National Park.
